collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — ADVICE AND DECISIONS (ADV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Asking for advice, giving it, ignoring it, following half of it, and deciding alone. Advice can be wrong, even from elders and experts. Following it doesn't guarantee a good outcome and ignoring it doesn't cause a bad one. Feeling heard with no decision is a perfectly good ending, and nobody ever has to admit someone else was right.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 7-12 and an adult)

collection.description: A child chosen to pick teams worries about leaving someone out: an adult gives an answer, or asks what the child thinks is fair.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has been chosen to pick the teams for the children's game this afternoon. (subject.He/she) is worried. If (subject.he/she) picks (subject.his/her) friends first, the others will feel bad. If (subject.he/she) doesn't pick (subject.his/her) friends, they'll feel bad. (subject.He/she) asks (friend) what to do.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Alternate," says (friend). "Pick a fast one, then a slow one, then a fast one." (subject) tries it. One child points out loudly that (other.he/she) has been picked as a "slow one." (subject) is mortified. They end up drawing names out of a bowl instead, which everyone agrees is fairest. (friend) admits that (friend.his/her) idea wasn't great.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "What do you think would be fairest?" asks (friend). (subject) thinks hard. "Maybe everyone picks a shell from a bowl, and the color says the team?" "Try it," says (friend). (subject) tries it. Nobody feels picked last. One child cries because (other.he/she) wanted the blue shells. You can't win them all.
